newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Shooting at funeral in strike-bound Karachi.
newsitem.headline: Shooting at funeral in strike-bound Karachi.

text.p: Gunmen ambushed the funeral of a political activist in Pakistan's strike-bound port city of Karachi on Sunday, killing a mourner and wounding at least eight, police said.
Unidentified attackers killed Yusuf Sultan as the funeral procession of activist Mohammad Hassan moved to a graveyard in Karachi's Malir district, a police official said.
Nobody claimed responsibility for the ambush during the day-long general strike, called by nine opposition groups to protest at alleged killings of political activists by police.
The police, who deny the charge, said a 40-year-old man, Mohammad Hanif, was also tortured and hanged on Sunday by unknown captors who disposed of his body in the city's District Central.
At least two vehicles were set on fire at Korangi in District East, apparently as a warning to drivers to keep their vehicles off the roads, police said.
The strike squeezed Pakistan's normally bustling commercial hub. Witnesses said shopping centres, schools and colleges were closed and public transport was at a standstill.
Government departments, airline offices at Karachi airport, the port and railways were open, but attendance was thin due to lack of transport, one witness said.
The Karachi Stock Exchange closed 9.34 points, or 0.69 percent, up despite the strike owing to technical correction and short-covering, dealers said.
The Karachi Cotton Association and Pakistan Yarn Merchants Association did not issue rates, however, because of thin attendance.
The strike also slowed the movement of petroleum products, edible oils and other food commodities to the countryside due to the fear of arson, one transport operator said.
A police official said the strike was only partial and that shops opened later in the day. He said most of the shops had closed their shutters for fear of violence.
Armed police and paramilitary rangers patrolled the city's violence-prone areas, witnesses said.
About 300 people have been killed in ethnic, sectarian and political violence in Karachi so far this year, far fewer than the 2,000 deaths recorded last year.

The nine-party opposition alliance, including the main Pakistan Muslim League and the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM), called the strike to protest at the killing by police of an MQM activist on Thursday.

Police said earlier that the activist, Mohammad Farooq, and other "terrorists" had attacked a police unit in Karachi's central Gulbhar area. Farooq was killed when police fired back and the others escaped.
The MQM seeks greater political and economic rights for Mohajirs, the Urdu-speaking Moslems who migrated from India when the subcontinent was partitioned in 1947, and their descendants.
